newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore weekly mid-distillates data correct- TDB.
newsitem.headline: Singapore weekly mid-distillates data correct- TDB.

text.p: Singapore's Trade Development Board (TDB) said on Monday that the level of middle distillate stocks in its weekly data last week was correct.
Last Thursday the TDB reported that middle distillate stocks had grown to 1.9 billion barrels compared with a week earlier 10.54 million barrels.
The latest data covered stocks onshore Singapore as of June 9.
"We wish to confirm that the data on middle distillates released on Thursday, 5 June 1997 is correct," the statement said in response to a Reuter query.
Traders in Singapore questioned the level of middle distillates reported by the TDB, saying it was far too high.
Singapore's capacity to store that amount of middle distillates, let alone all products, was a just a fraction of 1.9 billion barrels, they said.
They estimated storage capacity at slightly more than 3.5 million cubic meters, or 22 million barrels.
Traders said a straightforward comparison with the United States, or Japan, raised questions about the figure.
Last Tursday, the American Petroleum Institute showed that distillate stocks -- comparable to Singapore's middle distillates -- totalled 107.315 million barrels.
All oil stocks were 671.354 million barrels.

In Japan, the latest government statistics showed total oil product stocks at the end of April were 91.356 million barrels, including kerosene stocks at 17.23 million and gas oil at 15.41 million barrels.
